correctness.rationale: All coefficients, signs, zeros, and n≥2 are accounted for. For an arbitrary bounded set the exact radius follows from intersection of coordinate radius intervals with the zero-weight-sum hyperplane. A supremizing sequence in a maximum-coefficient coordinate bounds both signed weighted extrema by (W−bmax)diam. The n-point witness reaches this value and the universal half-diameter bound. This proves the theorem analytically. The bundled standard-library checker passed 52,800 exact rational assertions; an independent SciPy linear-program test passed 1,200 signed-coefficient instances. Tests support, not substitute for, the all-input proof.

originality.rationale: The exact maximum-norm hyperplane Jung radius formula, its finite extremizers, and all-weight threshold were compared by mathematical statement with the most relevant indexed findings and accessible primary full texts. Kobos characterizes maximal *linear projection* norms and provides the equal-weight benchmark, not an arbitrary-set Chebyshev-radius formula. Amir, Vesely and Castillo–Papini give general Jung theory, center existence, and finite Jung properties without the inspected all-coefficient equality. Franchetti 1977 and Bayod–Masa 1990 have incomplete full text, so hidden equivalent coverage remains possible; this risk is explicitly retained, not treated as disproved by a failed search.
residual_risks: Franchetti (1977) full text was not accessible; an implicit equivalent weighted-hyperplane Jung identity cannot be ruled out.
Bayod–Masa (1990) full text was not accessible; only the first page/abstract was available, so intermediate Jung coefficient estimates remain unverified.
Classical books on finite-dimensional polyhedral Banach geometry may contain the exact formula under an alternative name.

value.rationale: The family is natural: every codimension-one section of a finite-dimensional sup-norm cube by a linear hyperplane. Intrinsic radius/diameter loss measures the failure of metric-center preservation/injectivity under the section, an important Banach-space-geometric stability invariant. The all-coefficient formula is a sharp full classification with a geometric coefficient-dominance transition, explicit n-point extremizers and identification of all equal-weight maximizers. This goes beyond rephrasing known universal bounds or an isolated arbitrary finite computation.
